groups.instructions: Choose the correct option to complete each sentence.

questions.explanation: General truths use the zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple.

questions.prompt: If the council builds more cycle lanes, more people ______ to work by bike.
questions.explanation: A real, likely future result uses the first conditional: if + present, will + verb.

questions.prompt: If governments ______ fast food advertising, childhood obesity might decrease.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical present or future idea uses the second conditional: if + past simple, would/might + verb.

questions.prompt: If the bridge had been inspected regularly, the accident ______.
questions.explanation: An imagined different past uses the third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: If I ______ you, I would apply for the scholarship.
questions.explanation: In formal English, 'were' is used for all persons in the second conditional, especially in 'If I were you'.

questions.prompt: ______ the internet existed, people relied on libraries for information.
questions.explanation: This is a time clause, not a condition. 'Unless', 'if' and 'provided' express conditions and do not make sense here.

questions.prompt: You will not be allowed into the exam ______ you bring your passport.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if ... not': you will not be allowed in if you do not bring your passport.

questions.prompt: If she had studied medicine, she ______ a doctor now.
questions.explanation: A mixed conditional links a past condition (had studied) to a present result (would be ... now).

questions.prompt: ______ the government invest more in research, new treatments could be developed sooner.
questions.explanation: Inverted 'Should + subject + base verb' is a formal way of saying 'If the government invests ...'. 'Were' would need 'to invest'.

groups.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.

questions.prompt: If taxes on fuel rose, people {{10}} (drive) less.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: If more trees {{11}} (plant) in the past, the floods would have been less severe.
questions.explanation: Third conditional in the passive: if + had been + past participle.

questions.prompt: Unless action {{12}} (take) soon, many species will disappear.
questions.explanation: In first-conditional clauses (if/unless), use the present tense even for the future, here in the passive: is taken.
